$what: DRAFT when-rules for the dashboard's parts (R5's 18, derived by script from the two dashboard templates' $composes + the #261 metas) plus the dashboard frame, and the four parts observation C touches. NOT IN CANON. Dave rules the wording on Tuesday 29 September.
$how_to_enact: On his yes, for each row with change != KEEP: set the meta's `when` to `proposed` (a plain string replace of one field; rows marked AMEND append clauses to the gate half and keep the prose half byte-identical), add the `registry` fields to knowledge/when-fields.json `fields` by addition (s273-D4 lets a lane add a name with its definition and example), then run the yieldsTo derivation and knowledge/_validate_roles_resolve.py (check 10 when-fields-known). check_drafts.py in this folder rehearses every step on a scratch copy.

needs.definition: what the person must do to the records as a set (`sort`, `filter`, `select`, `edit`; `none` = they only read them)

layout.grammar.definition: the layout grammar the page is built on (`bento` = canon's bento-of-bentos, s217-D2; `grid` = the layout-utilities grid)

interrupts.definition: whether the moment must stop the person until they answer (`required` = a confirmation or a task that cannot share the screen; `none` = the choice can be made in place)

actions.definition: how many related actions hang off one trigger

options.definition: how many choices one selection offers

rows.current: destinations <= 7 AND nav.levels <= 2 — the default for dashboards — the bento template composes it; beats app-shell-side-nav (roles.json when: "> 7 destinations or two nav levels") below those bounds and app-shell-nav-rail (when: "dense app, content cannot spare 248px") when the content can spare the column; yields to app-shell-multi-column (when: "list-and-detail job") and to app-shell-focused (when: "one job, no navigation (auth, wizard)") when the job has no navigation. Co-providers of page-frame are mutually exclusive by construction (roles.json §05: one-at-a-time facility), so no not-with is authored.

rows.current: emphasis in (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary) AND label = text — the default of the role; yields to icon-button (roles.json when: "space is tight and the glyph is universal") when label = glyph, to split-button (when: "one main action plus a menu of related ones") when a menu hangs off the action, and to links (when: "the action is navigation inside running text") when the action is navigation in prose.

rows.current: records >= 2 AND the records are the same kind, each read ACROSS its own row AND surface in (none, bordered-per-record) — surface ALONE decides the container (s274-D1): unbordered ⇒ simple-list (one line per record) or structured-list (aligned fields); a bordered surface drawn around EACH record ⇒ card-list. Actions are a ROW property, allowed in any of the three, so they decide nothing. No field count, row count or column count gates this (s274-D4): the comparison test decides — if a field must be read DOWN a column across records, it is a table, not a list. A list-level heading is OPTIONAL on all three containers (s274-D5); a per-card title is a ROW field, distinct from the list heading. Beats table (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly") and data-grid (when: "sort / filter / select / edit-in-place is required") whenever each record is read across its own row; yields to timeline (when: "time is the structure, records have happened") and to tree (when: "records nest").

AND layout.grammar = bento — the dashboard frame when the designer's answer to 'dashboard bento — is that right?' is yes (s230-D1 beat 2); its tiles are themselves bentos (s217-D2, s217-D3). rows.proposed: interrupts = required — the person must stop: confirm a consequential action, or finish a task that cannot share the screen; yields to split-button when interrupts = none AND actions >= 2 (one main action with a few related ones beside it), and to dropdown when interrupts = none AND options >= 5 (one choice from a list, made in place, s270-D1).
rows.why: Dave's third Thursday observation as a rule the graph can read (observation C).

rows.proposed: options >= 5 AND interrupts = none — one choice from a list, made in place (s270-D1: "we use dropdowns for 5 and above"); beats modals whenever the choice does not need to stop the person.
rows.why: Observation C, with Dave's own 5-and-above cut-off (s270-D1) as the count.
